2.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

3.meaning: The Most Gracious / All-Merciful (al-Raḥmān) — a name of Allah from the root of mercy, in an intensive pattern denoting mercy that is vast, all-encompassing, and overflowing to all creation.
3.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', written al-raḥmān, said ar-raḥmān). An intensive noun-form expressing immense, overflowing mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or name in apposition to such.

4.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: A linking phrase meaning 'and upon Him' or 'and on Him' — joining a statement to what precedes and pointing reliance, dependence, or obligation toward a single male (here, Allah).
6.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the preposition 'alā ('upon'). The preposition pulls its pronoun into the genitive, and the pronoun accordingly takes the -hi form meaning 'Him'. Placing 'upon Him' before its verb typically gives the sense 'upon Him (and none else)'.
6.root: — (particle/preposition; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: 'We have placed our trust, relied wholly (upon someone).' The root means to entrust an affair, to depend on and commit oneself; this pattern expresses fully delegating one's reliance. The subject is 'we.'
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive pattern ('to commit one's reliance, put one's trust'). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we put our trust').
7.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, commit an affair

8.meaning: 'Then you will soon come to know.' A verb of knowing addressed to a group, prefaced by 'then' and the near-future marker 'will soon', typically used as a warning that the truth of a matter will become plain.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'you (plural) know'. The 'ta-…-ūna' frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The prefix 'sa-' places it in the near future ('will soon'), and 'fa-' links it to what precedes ('then / so'). The retained final 'na' (in '-ūna') shows the indicative, a plain statement of fact. Often delivered as a threat or solemn warning.
8.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, to know

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

10.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
12.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
12.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

13.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
13.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A rhetorical address meaning roughly 'Have you considered?' or 'Tell me — what do you think of…?'. It combines the question particle 'a-' ('do/have…?') with the verb 'to see', here in the sense of mentally considering or reflecting on something rather than literal eyesight. It is addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying a subject built into its ending: the '-tum' ending marks a completed action done by 'you all' (masculine plural). Prefixed with the question particle 'a-', it turns the statement into a question, idiomatically 'have you considered / tell me'.

3.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
3.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'to become' or 'to enter the morning'. Literally it means to come into the morning/dawn, but it very commonly works as a 'becoming' verb: a thing comes to be in some new state.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -a ending with no further marker indicates a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he/it'. As one of the 'sisters of kāna' it often functions to assign a state ('became / came to be such-and-such'), describing a completed transition into a new condition.
4.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning, dawn, to enter upon morning

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'your water'. The noun 'water' joined to the possessor 'your (plural)' — water as the life-giving fluid, here belonging to a group of people.
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u case vowel (appearing before the suffix) is nominative, typically marking the subject or topic of a sentence. The suffix -kum means 'your' for a group (second-person masculine plural). So the form is 'your (all of you) water', positioned as a subject/topic.

6.meaning: Water that has sunk deep into the earth and vanished beyond reach; a sinking-away or draining-down of water so that none remains at the surface.
6.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative (manṣūb), marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). This ending commonly marks the object of a verb or the predicate of a 'becoming' verb ('it becomes ___'), describing the state into which something passes.
6.root: غ-و-ر (gh-w-r) — to sink, to go deep down; a hollow, the bottom of something

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
7.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

8.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'he comes to you / brings to you'. It combines the act of coming/arriving with delivering or bringing something to the addressee.
8.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb in Form I (the basic, unaugmented stem). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he/it' — note ya- (not yu-), which confirms Form I rather than the Form IV causative. The attached -kum is an object pronoun, 'you' (a plural group). The verb's base sense is 'to come', and with an object it carries the sense 'to come to / bring (something) to'. So the form signals 'he comes to / brings to you all'.
8.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

9.meaning: With water — by means of water, the clear liquid essential to life.
9.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with / by means of'. Because it is a preposition, the following noun takes the genitive: the -in ending here is genitive with indefiniteness ('nunation'), so 'with (some) water'.

10.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'flowing' or 'gushing' water — water that runs freely on the surface, easily reached and visible, as from a spring.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective. The -in (tanwīn kasra) ending marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness ('(some) flowing water'). The genitive typically appears after a preposition or when one noun is linked to another ('… OF …'), or describing such a noun. So this form is set up to follow a preposition or qualify a preceding genitive noun.
10.root: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye, spring, flowing source (or م-ع-ن, to flow)
